problem: Prior generalizable 3D feature fields (e.g., HNR) are supervised only by 2D foundation models such as CLIP/DINOv2. This gives weak 3D spatial understanding, a gap to language semantics, and poor understanding of long text over large-scale panorama/BEV representations.
motivation: Embodied agents need 3D representations that generalize to unseen scenes, update in real time and support open-vocabulary language queries. Feature fields meet these needs but lack language supervision. Large 3D-language datasets (SceneVerse, ScanRefer) now exist, so feature fields can be pre-trained with multi-granularity language.
key_idea: Pre-train a generalizable feature-field model (novel view, panorama and BEV renderings) on about 1M 3D-language annotations over 5K scenes, using multi-level contrastive learning: balanced object-level, fine-grained long-text and CLIP distillation.
insight: Both language supervision and CLIP distillation are needed: CLIP-only gives monocular VLN SR 44.6 and ObjNav SR 47.6 (Table ablation_CL), while the full model gives 47.2 and 55.6. The balanced object loss matters for small objects (ObjNav SR 51.7 unbalanced vs 55.6), and fine-grained long-text contrast beats a single [SEP] vector for VLN (SR 45.7 vs 47.2). Novel views drive monocular VLN gains (SR 33.1 to 46.9), while BEV alone hurts ObjNav because a local value map is also needed.
method: 3D-language data: about 5K scenes (ScanNet, HM3D, Structured3D) with about 1M annotations (SceneVerse, ScanRefer), retrievable via instance-level point-cloud IDs
Feature field encoding: following HNR, CLIP patch features are back-projected with depth into 3D points, storing orientation and region size, and updated online

Ray-View-Panorama encoding: MLP_view aggregates 4 nearest features (radius 0.5 m) and volume-renders a 12x12x768 view map. A view transformer and a panorama transformer over 12 views at 30° intervals then encode it
Ray-BEV encoding: vertical rays render a 168x168 BEV map covering 16.8x16.8 m, downsampled by a 7x7 conv to 24x24 and passed through a BEV transformer
Balanced object alignment: cross-entropy over a 1,883-category vocabulary, with the top-10% hardest rays up-weighted by a factor alpha

Fine-grained long-text contrastive: an affinity matrix between 5x5 BEV window (or panorama) features and CLIP word features, scored by the mean of the top-L similarities, trained with a bidirectional InfoNCE loss
CLIP distillation: contrastive loss against CLIP features of ground-truth views/regions for the view, panorama and BEV outputs
Downstream integration: replaces the feature fields in VLN-3DFF (monocular VLN) and HNR (panorama VLN); serves as the value map source in VLFM (object navigation); provides three decoders for SQA3D

setting.backbone: g3D-LF feature fields (CLIP ViT features + MLPs + 4-layer transformer encoders, trained) plugged into VLN-3DFF / HNR / VLFM / SQA3D-style decoders
setting.training_data: About 5K indoor scenes (ScanNet, HM3D, Structured3D) with about 1M language annotations (SceneVerse, ScanRefer); train splits only; pre-trained for 50K episodes (about 10 days on 2 RTX 6000 Ada)
setting.observation: Posed RGB-D images (monocular forward view or 12-view panorama)
setting.action_space: Predicted candidate waypoints on a topological graph (VLN); frontier/waypoint selection with a point-goal policy (ObjNav)
setting.simulator: Habitat (R2R-CE, HM3D, MP3D); ScanNet for SQA3D
setting.privileged: none (poses and depth from the simulator, as is standard in these benchmarks)

numbers_note: The SQA3D table does not state which split is used; 'test' is assumed. The ObjNav splits are the validation splits described in the text.
results: g3D-LF raises monocular R2R-CE val-unseen SR from 44.9 (VLN-3DFF) to 47.2 and SPL from 30.4 to 34.6. In the panorama setting it ties HNR on SR (61) and reaches SOTA SPL (52). Zero-shot ObjNav SPL is 31.8 on HM3D and 18.8 on MP3D, beating VLFM (30.4 and 17.5), and localization on SQA3D is much better than SQA3D-baseline (Acc@0.5m 23.4 vs 14.6).
limitations: Cannot handle dynamic environments where objects or people move, and has not been tested on manipulation
The scale and quality of 3D-language data remain limited; SQA3D answer accuracy (EM@1 47.7) trails LLM-based methods (Scene-LLM 54.2)
Gains in the panorama VLN setting are minor, and BEV rendering is slow (about 6 FPS); the object vocabulary is limited to 1,883 categories
